extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing and submitting preprints to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting an article to arXiv, including permitted file formats, metadata, file-naming rules, figure handling, timing/announcement rules, and policies on edits and responsibility. Aimed at authors who will upload source or compiled files to the arXiv submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitters only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone who submits should read the general information. Also see special instructions for third party submission and index submissions for conference proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: No omitted figures/tables/sections or 'abstract only' submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are unhelpful to readers and of very limited archival value. Do not provide only links to figures on another server; omitted figures are not accepted even if linked externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; DOCX (Word 2007); PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to store articles in formats which are highly portable and stable over time. Currently, the best choice is TeX/LaTeX, because this open format does not hide information. Note that for this and other reasons we will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Users of word processors such as Microsoft Word (versions prior to Word 2007) should save their documents as PDF and submit that. Scanned documents are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in a number of common formats: PostScript (PS/EPS, most common for line drawings, plots, etc.), JPEG (ideal for photographic images), GIF or PNG (best for non-photographic images, bitmaps), PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections may not be able to download them; reduce size when possible. See information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators. arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures even if you provide a link to another server.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. These restrictions ensure maximum portability of the stored files and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name and extension case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on our system; internal file references must match case exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same. Whether your local system is case sensitive (e.g. Unix) or not (e.g. Windows) you must ensure that internal file references such as LaTeX figure inclusion commands match case exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) which are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate title/abstract preparation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching. See separate instructions on the preparation of separate title/abstract information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read messages before final submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making the final 'Submit Article' step, check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting then correct them or contact arXiv administrators if there are problems you cannot resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit to correct errors before public announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to the incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting an article takes the article out of the processing queue and announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits, versioning and replacement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. Do not make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum; rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed. Edits and final submission before 16:00 US Eastern time Monday through Friday will not delay announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must take responsibility; third-party submission discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because putting articles on arXiv entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement schedule and ordering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv are normally announced on a daily schedule, with no activity scheduled on weekends. Submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in the listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A submission made on Monday before 16:00 US Eastern will be publicly available after 20:00 US Eastern that day and appear in the Tuesday AM subject mailing. A submission made on Friday before 16:00 will be publicly available after 20:00 of the following Sunday. A submission made on Friday at or after 16:00 will be publicly available after 20:00 of the following Monday. An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset submission time and thus change position in the listings. Edits are permitted between 16:00 and the 20:00 announcement time; however doing this will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: If including figures in LaTeX source, use standard macro packages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues, so seek help from your colleagues if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size considerations and network accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, then readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure to include large figures but make all possible efforts to reduce their size. Note arXiv has many users with poor network connections (such as users in some developing nations). See information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.
